newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares firm 0.3 pct to fresh record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares firm 0.3 pct to fresh record.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's stock exchange edged higher despite profit-taking on Tuesday to reach its fifth consecutive record, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed at a new all-time high of 78,711.82, up 232.11 points, or 0.3 percent from Monday's 78,479.71, the previous record.
Trade volume dropped to 19.32 trillion lira from yesterday's 25.79 trillion lira which included a 3.5 trillion lira block deal on the wholesale market.

"The market recovered to test the 79,000 barrier again after the morning profit-taking. Activity was led by shares which carried less premiums than others. Shares were being switched," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
The index was down 0.17 percent at midday. It brushed a high of 79,378 in hectic afternoon trade but fell back in profit-taking. It was the second test of the 79,000 resistance after Monday.
Brokers said the market still awaited a correction to the continuing medium-term uptrend. The index has surged 21.5 percent since mid-September.

Of the 227 shares traded, 130 declined, 61 rose and 36 finished steady. The 85-share industrial index gained 0.3 percent to 84,678.03 and the 15-share financial index firmed 0.29 percent to 73,113.54.

Actives were led by T.Isbank's C series shares, up 500 lira at 13,000, utility Aktas Elektrik, down 3,000 lira at 63,000 and largely state owned firms slated for privatisation -- petroleum distributor Petrol Ofisi, up 2,000 lira at 29,500 and flat steel producer Eregli, down 100 lira at 9,900. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875
